claim: SambaNova DataScale SN3000 is an ASIC-based data center inference accelerator using custom RDU (Rainbow Dataflow Unit) architecture with on-chip SRAM instead of external GPU memory. Single-chip LLM inference throughput claimed at 300-3000+ tok/s depending on model size. Independent verification limited — primarily vendor claims from sambanova.ai.

specs.memory: On-chip SRAM (no external memory); chip-level SRAM capacity varies by configuration; architecture eliminates memory wall by using dataflow execution with SRAM at compute
specs.compute: Custom RDU (Rainbow Dataflow Unit) ASIC; optimized for INT8/FP8 inference; throughput not expressed in traditional TFLOPS — vendor uses tokens/sec as primary metric
specs.throughput: 300-3000+ tok/s single-stream depending on model size (8B-70B+); designed for low-latency single-stream inference at scale

price_usd: Not publicly listed; data center pricing typically $50K-150K per node (estimates from vendor contacts); sold as complete DataScale systems (not per-chip)
notes: SambaNova lacks independent third-party benchmark verification. All throughput claims come from vendor documentation. The architecture is fundamentally different from GPUs — ASIC with on-chip SRAM eliminates memory bandwidth bottleneck for single-stream inference. However, multi-stream aggregate throughput and flexibility (model switching, fine-tuning) are unverified. The system is sold as complete DataScale racks, not individual chips, making direct price comparison difficult. Confidence is low due to limited independent sources.
key_differentiator: On-chip SRAM eliminates memory wall; deterministic low-latency single-stream inference
limitations: Pricing not public; sold as complete systems
ASIC — less flexible than GPU for model switching
Limited ecosystem compared to NVIDIA CUDA
